justification: Data-only triage of the 5 chapters the 2026-07-29 preflight (#844/#849) flagged SUSPECT for two-column interleave, sitting >48h in the review queue as pre-existing backlog (blacktown 36 / cos 105 / georges_river 6+31 / hornsby 25 pending rows — none from today's work). Downloaded each chapter's current R2 PDF and sampled multiple body pages (not just TOC) through the actual detect_two_column_words/preflight_layout functions already shipped. Verdict: blacktown + georges_river (both chapters) are false positives — every body page sampled reads as clean single-column prose; the detector trips on heavily indented lettered/numbered sub-item lists. hornsby is a genuine interleave — a 'Note:' sidebar column mixes mid-sentence into body text on multiple pages. city_of_sydney is genuine too but already handled (in GEOMETRIC_COLUMN_COUNCILS since #844) — left untouched; its real issue is unrelated pre-existing garbage refs from map/figure pages, out of scope for this pass. Two additive changes: blacktown + georges_river added to PREFLIGHT_TWO_COL_VERIFIED (Waverley-precedent — flag suppressed once evidenced); hornsby added to GEOMETRIC_COLUMN_COUNCILS (extraction now reads it column-aware; the SUSPECT flag deliberately stays, matching CoS, since no full fidelity sweep has proven it yet).

pre_impl.existing_data: Both constants (GEOMETRIC_COLUMN_COUNCILS, PREFLIGHT_TWO_COL_VERIFIED) and the geometric columnar reader already exist and are unmodified; this only extends the two membership sets with evidence from real PDFs downloaded from production R2.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A false-positive verdict from limited page sampling would wrongly suppress a real warning; mitigated by sampling multiple non-adjacent body pages per chapter (not just the first) and checking the extracted text reads as coherent prose in order.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Pure additive: two set-literal entries, no new functions, no logic change.

functions: N/A — no functions added or modified; existing detect_two_column_words/preflight_layout unchanged.

values.if_missing: both chapters keep re-flagging SUSPECT forever with no path to clear the backlog despite the content being fine

values.read_at: scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py, consulted at DCPExtractor column-read dispatch (~line 1009)

break_it.scenario: A future hornsby chapter's Note-sidebar pattern differs enough that the geometric gutter finder misreads it.
break_it.what_happens: _find_gutter/_columnar_text return None per-page on any non-two-column page (existing fallback), so worst case is plain single-column reading order for that page — never worse than before this change.
break_it.how: Same fallback already proven for ashfield/marrickville/city_of_sydney; no new code path.
break_it.repro: N/A — existing behaviour, not introduced here.

break_it.scenario: blacktown or georges_river later genuinely gains two-column content in an amendment.
break_it.what_happens: The SUSPECT flag stays suppressed for that council even though the new content needs review.
break_it.how: Accepted risk, same as the pre-existing Waverley exemption — the count-drop/schema-fail/coverage gates still catch content loss independently of the layout flag.
break_it.repro: N/A — documented risk pattern, not testable in isolation.
